definitions.explanation: A speech sound produced without vibration of the vocal cords. In Japanese, the voiceless consonants include the k, s, t, h, and p series, written with basic kana without diacritical marks.

examples.japanese: ⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧「p」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧「b」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無声音|むせいおん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{有声音|ゆうせいおん}→有声音：26420_yuuseion⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対|つい}→対：00411_tsui⟧だ。
examples.english: The English "p" and "b" are a pair of voiceless and voiced sounds.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{母音|ぼいん}→母音：13205_boin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{挟|はさ}まれた→挟む：00091_hasamu⟧{無声音|むせいおん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{有声化|ゆうせいか}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese, voiceless sounds between vowels sometimes become voiced.

notes:
A compound of {無声|むせい} (voiceless, without voice) and {音|おん} (sound). The antonym of ⟦{有声音|ゆうせいおん}→有声音：26420_yuuseion⟧ (voiced sound). Voiceless sounds are produced by airflow through the mouth without the vocal cords vibrating.

JAPANESE VOICELESS CONSONANT SERIES:
- {か行|かぎょう} (ka, ki, ku, ke, ko): voiceless velar
- {さ行|さぎょう} (sa, shi, su, se, so): voiceless alveolar
- {た行|たぎょう} (ta, chi, tsu, te, to): voiceless dental
- {は行|はぎょう} (ha, hi, fu, he, ho): voiceless glottal/bilabial
- {ぱ行|ぱぎょう} (pa, pi, pu, pe, po): voiceless bilabial

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無声音|むせいおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子音|しいん}→子音：18405_shiin⟧: voiceless consonant
- {無声音|むせいおん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{有声音|ゆうせいおん}→有声音：26420_yuuseion⟧: voiceless and voiced sounds
- {無声|むせい}{破裂音|はれつおん}: voiceless plosive

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{有声音|ゆうせいおん}→有声音：26420_yuuseion⟧: voiced sound — the opposite; produced with vocal cord vibration
- ⟦{清音|せいおん}→清音：23458_seion⟧: voiceless kana — the traditional Japanese term for basic unmarked kana
- ⟦{濁音|だくおん}→濁音：19295_dakuon⟧: voiced kana — kana marked with dakuten
